bottleneck: Children acquire language effortlessly during a critical period whose neural basis is unknown: what changes in the brain to close the window — inhibitory circuit maturation, molecular brakes like perineuronal nets, or something else — and whether it can be safely reopened are open questions. Adult language learning never reaches native proficiency, limiting global communication, immigrant integration, and rehabilitation after brain injury. The critical period is one of the most replicated findings in neuroscience and also one of the least explained: described in detail, understood barely at all.
current_state: Research implicates inhibitory circuit maturation and molecular brakes, but no intervention safely reopens language plasticity in humans, and the closure trigger is unidentified.
title: Language critical period mechanism unknown
why_it_blocks: Understanding the window would transform education, enable language recovery after stroke, and reveal how the brain's learning machinery is scheduled. A fundamental capacity of the human brain runs on an unknown timer.
